text:
Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake: How to Beat BOTH Shooting Galleries
The Shooting Gallery is one of the many minigames you'll encounter in The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, offering valuable rewards like bigger Deku Seed Bags and Quivers, along with an easy way to earn extra Rupees. There are two locations to visit: one in Castle Town as a child and another in Kakariko Village as an adult. Both feature Basic and Expert difficulties, with increasingly challenging targets to hit.
 
In this guide, we'll show you how to win both Shooting Gallery minigames, explain the target patterns, and share helpful tips for improving your aim. We'll also explain why Gyro Controls can make a huge difference, how the randomized targets work in Kakariko Village, and how to earn all the available rewards. With these tips, you'll be hitting every target in no time!

James Gunn, Peter Safran Out at DC Studios - IGN Daily Fix
In today's Daily Fix:
DC Studios co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran are out, in a massive shakeup in Skydance media subsidiaries. The announcement was made by owner Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kriez. Gunn and Safran will be replaced by Jeremy Latcham, who previously worked as a producer with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy for Marvel. Gunn and Safran will stay on in producer roles on projects already in the works at DC Studios. This follows an up and down year for the rebooted film studio, with strong box office returns and reviews for James Gunn's Superman last year, but a massive bomb with this year's Supergirl. Clayface was a modest hit, and their HBO fare has been widely acclaimed. Gunn is still in the middle of post-production on next year's Man of Tomorrow. In other news, Godzilla: Minus Zero opened to a titanic $64 million weekend worlwide, making it the biggest debut for a live-action foreign film ever. And in gaming news, Sony is launching a new model of the PlayStation Portal in Japan, and this could be the next step in a new full-fledged PlayStation gaming handheld.

The 9th Dragon - Official Announcement Trailer
Take a look at the announcement trailer for The 9th Dragon, an upcoming side-scroller beat 'em up action adventure game. The 9th Dragon combines tactical combat with a dynamic free-style beat ‘em up approach as players navigate the gritty neon maze of Kowloon as Rookie, the newest member of an elite police commando unit. Players will shape the narrative to go either way - will Rookie be a hero, or not? It all depends on the decisions made throughout the story. You can learn more about The 9th Dragon on Steam if you're interested: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4402330/The_9th_Dragon/

The 9th Dragon will be available on PC (Epic Games Store and Steam), PlayStation, Xbox, and Nintendo Switch.

author: IGN YouTube
text:
Criminal - Official Teaser Trailer (2027) Charlie Hunnam, Luke Evans, Emilia Clarke
Check out the teaser trailer for Criminal, an upcoming series featuring an interlocking universe of crime stories based on the multi-Eisner Award-winning graphic novel series created by Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips’ bestselling graphic novel series of the same name. Criminal stars Charlie Hunnam, Adria Arjona, Luke Evans, Emilia Clarke, Richard Jenkins, Kadeem Hardison, Gus Halper, John Hawkes, and Logan Browning. The recurring and guest cast includes Michael Mando, Garrett Hedlund, Patrick J. Adams, Pat Healy, Taylor Selé, Aliyah Camacho, Marvin Jones III, Michael Xavier, Dominic Burgess, Chris Diamantopoulos, Lawrence Kao, Katie Stevens, John Pyper-Ferguson, Robert Lee Hart, Aina Brei'yon and Kyle Davis.

Criminal begins with the story of two friends, Leo Patterson (Charlie Hunnam) and Ricky Lawless (Gus Halper), one trying to fight his way out of the world of crime they were raised in, the other desperate to follow in the footsteps of his father, a legendary outlaw. And when Ricky's older brother Tracy (Luke Evans) returns home from the Army, their tragic family history comes home with him. Drawn into their orbit are Greta (Adria Arjona), a sharp-tongued car thief from Leo’s past, and Mallory (Emilia Clarke), Ricky's girlfriend, who fears what he'll do to get by. Gunfights, heists, and tragic romance are the order of the day, but will anyone make it out alive?

Criminal is based on the graphic novels by Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips, and executive produced by Brubaker, Phillips, Philipp A. Barnett, Anna Boden, Ryan Fleck, Jordan Harper, Sarah Carbiener, Dee Rees, and Halley Gross, along with co-executive producers Cortney Norris and Minhal Baig. It is produced by Amazon MGM Studios, Basement Gang, Inc., Big Indie Pictures, Inc., Gowanus Projections, Inc., and Legendary Television Productions, Inc.

All four episodes of Criminal Part One “Coward” will debut on January 13, 2027, followed by all four episodes of Criminal Part Two “Lawless” on January 27, 2027 on Prime Video.
